tech_stack: Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 WebFlux / Reactive Event-Driven Stream Processing

module_layout.integration: Single deployable, single composition root. Intake publishes TelemetrySampleValidated, TelemetrySampleValidationFailed, TelemetryBackfillReordered and TelemetryWindowBuffered through a bounded in-process reactive event bridge (Sinks.many().multicast().onBackpressureBuffer, capacity and overflow strategy externalized). Ledger subscribes to validation outcomes only (customer-supplier), never calls Intake and never re-validates or reorders. Intake is an anticorruption layer toward edge devices (Ingress Packet -> Telemetry Sample) and an open host service toward downstream analytics streams (published language, backpressure-aware Flux broadcast). Ledger-side recording is eventual, retried, and never blocks intake; unrecoverable records go to a dead-letter sink.

build_order: shared (externalized configuration properties: sensor metric boundaries, reorder window duration, buffer capacities, overflow strategy, retry/timeout, clock bean)
intake.domain (Telemetry Sample, Ingress Packet, Sensor Metric Boundary, validation status, reorder window state)
intake.application (validation, 60s reorder by t_device, windowed buffering, broadcasting ports)
ledger.application (append and revision use cases, read/query use cases)
intake.infrastructure (bounded sinks, event bridge, boundary policy preload, stream subscription lifecycle)
ledger.infrastructure (reactive repository adapter, entity mappings, data-access config, event subscription adapter with retry and DLQ)
intake.api (ingestion endpoint with backpressure, windowed telemetry stream endpoint)
ledger.api (history and revision read endpoints, ProblemDetail error mapping)
integration wiring and end-to-end StepVerifier/WebTestClient tests
risks: Handling of packets later than the 60s reorder window (reject vs accept as revision) is unspecified; default to appending a revision and make the policy configurable
Reorder window state is in-memory; a restart loses unflushed window contents
Burst loads may overflow bounded sinks; overflow strategy must be explicit and observable, with no sample silently dropped before validation tagging
Ledger append failure must not block intake; needs retry with backoff and a dead-letter sink
Downstream consumer identity, device authentication and athlete/session ownership are undefined
High write rate against append-only store requires batching and avoiding heavy indexes on the write path
Boundary values (HR 30-240, power 0-2500, cadence 0-220, swim pace >45 s/100m) must come from configuration, not literals

drivers: Ledger owns the data; Intake keeps only in-memory reorder window state
persistence.storage_paradigm: Durable relational store with append-only, time-ordered event log semantics; high write rate, no updates or deletes of raw records
persistence.data_model: Telemetry Record Event: identity, device, metric type, value, device timestamp, ingress timestamp, validation status, payload retained, revision number, revision reason (original, correction, backfill), recorded-at. Revisions append new rows referencing the original record; uniqueness over (record identity, revision number).
queries: Record history by device and device-timestamp range ordered by t_device
All revisions of one record in revision order (audit trail)
persistence.migration_plan: Expand-only schema migrations versioned and run at startup; embeddable in-process substitute for tests
persistence.backup_recovery: Periodic snapshots plus log-based point-in-time recovery; append-only history makes replay safe and idempotent
open_questions: Retention and partitioning policy for long-term 1Hz history
Treatment of backfilled frames beyond the 60s window
